question: After the WhatsApp parity defect is fixed, should these shared authorization and secret-registry builders become the canonical public Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The new helpers centralize sensitive authorization and credential-discovery semantics while adding public plugin API surface, so their permanent contract and defaults require explicit owner intent.

options.title: Fix parity and approve APIs
options.body: Restore all migrated inputs, add focused regressions and live proof, then adopt the public helpers as canonical.

options.title: Keep security helpers internal
options.body: Share the implementation for bundled channels without publishing authorization or secret-registry builders yet.

options.title: Split lower-risk helpers
options.body: Land config-hint and directory helpers separately while holding authorization and secret-registry work for focused review.

recommendation.title: Fix parity and approve APIs
recommendation.body: Restore all migrated inputs, add focused regressions and live proof, then adopt the public helpers as canonical.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged native-approval work provides the strongest available ownership signal for shared approval SDK boundaries and channel-parity review.
